summary: Evaluation of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS closed-loop data shows strong overall glycemic control with an 86.0% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), a low coefficient of variation (32.6%), and active Oref1 automation utilizing SMB, UAM, and dynamic sensitivity. Mild vulnerability to nocturnal dipping and late afternoon elevations is present, operating under a pure UAM and microbolus paradigm due to the absence of explicit carbohydrate logging.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is exceptional at 98.7% over 14 days with 3,995 valid entries and stable 5-minute cadence. Telemetry completeness is robust with active closed-loop statuses and treatment logs.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries, 98.7% coverage, 655 insulin entries totaling 275.95 U, maximum data gap of 65 minutes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carb treatment entries count is 0 in telemetry summary, reflecting a pure UAM/uncarbed operational style.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic control is very good with 86.0% TIR and low variability (CV 32.6%), though Time Below Range at 5.1% slightly exceeds standard safety thresholds (<4%), driven by mild nocturnal and early morning dipping.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, CV 32.6%, glucose extremes reaching lows of 41-42 mg/dL and highs up to 293 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of explicit carb logs limits direct correlation between low events and unannounced activity or stacking.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates maintain stable fasting levels but show occasional dipping below 70 mg/dL during local hours 00:00-01:00 (11% to 18.5% TBR). Afternoon hours (15:00-17:00) show elevated glucose excursions averaging 153-162 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly glucose metrics showing local hour 0-1 average 90-93 mg/dL with 11-18.5% TBR; local hour 15-16 average 153-162 mg/dL with 23-32% TAR.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unrecorded meal intake makes separating afternoon basal drift from unannounced meal impact difficult.

analysis_steps.findings: The profile uses a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, a 10-hour DIA, and multi-segment CR. Oref1 dynamic sensitivity (70% adjustment factor) actively compresses or expands effective ISF to compensate for the flat static profile.
analysis_steps.evidence: Active Aaps profile configuration: ISF 56 mg/dL/U, DIA 10 hours, CR segments ranging from 10.5 to 13.2 g/U, dynamic ISF enabled at 70%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of recorded carb entries prevents direct validation of CR segment accuracy.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled with SMB always enabled and permitted under temporary targets. Delivery is configured with a 3-minute interval and conservative basal safety caps, supporting responsive unannounced meal management.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS settings: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true, smb_with_temp_target_enabled=true, smb_interval_minutes=3 min.

analysis_steps.findings: Static Autosens is disabled while dynamic sensitivity is active at 70%, allowing real-time ISF adaptation. Safety limits (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) provide wide safety margins well above actual peak loop enactments.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70%, max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h, max_iob_units=25 U.

analysis_steps.findings: Without manual carb entries or explicit meal bolus declarations, insulin delivery relies entirely on Oref1 UAM detection, microboluses, and manual correction boluses.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries=0, total_carbs_g=0.0, therapy response windows showing correction bolus responses over 240-360 minutes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of meal carb declarations and prebolus timing.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carb entries and e-carb durations are unpopulated. Active GLP-1 therapy notes (1.25mg) and a 7-hour max absorption window support delayed gastric emptying and prolonged absorption handling by UAM.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries=0, meal_max_absorption_hours=7.0 h, GLP-1 1.25mg administration notes in representative events.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No detailed meal composition or explicit e-carb scheduling data.

analysis_steps.findings: The closed-loop system performs effectively under a pure UAM/microbolus strategy. Profile settings and automation parameters are mutually consistent and safe, requiring no immediate parameter alterations.
analysis_steps.evidence: High TIR (86.0%), stable dynamic sensitivity adjustments, and conservative safety caps supported by 14 days of high-quality telemetry.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of carbohydrate logging limits precision in evaluating CR and meal-matching.

strengths: High Time in Range (86.0%) and low glycemic variability (CV 32.6%) across the 14-day period.
Robust CGM data quality with 98.7% coverage and stable 5-minute cadence.
Well-calibrated Oref1 automation settings (SMB enabled, UAM enabled, dynamic sensitivity at 70%) providing reliable closed-loop adaptation.
Conservative safety limits (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) preventing algorithmic restriction while maintaining safety ceilings.
issues: Time Below Range (5.1%) slightly exceeds the standard <4% target, driven by mild nocturnal/early morning dipping during local hours 00:00-01:00.
Late afternoon glucose elevations (local hours 15:00-17:00) averaging 153-162 mg/dL with reduced time in range (~67-75%).
Absence of explicit carbohydrate logging limits the ability to evaluate postprandial insulin-to-carb matching.

recommendations.title: Monitor Overnight Low Trends
recommendations.description: Observe overnight glucose trajectories during local hours 00:00-01:00 where time below range reaches up to 18.5%, ensuring Oref1 low-temp enactments continue to prevent severe hypoglycemia without requiring immediate basal rate changes.

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Automation Configuration
recommendations.description: Keep current SMB, UAM, and dynamic sensitivity settings active without modification, as they successfully compensate for unannounced meal absorption and GLP-1 therapy effects.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Current basal segments, CR profiles, ISF, and DIA are operating effectively within an automated Oref1 loop, achieving an 86% TIR. Observed mild dipping and afternoon elevations are adequately managed by dynamic sensitivity and UAM without requiring structural profile edits.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose trends and afternoon postprandial levels for 5-7 days before considering any rate adjustments.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current profile and automation settings unchanged while observing nocturnal low trends.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Maintains stable overnight fasting levels. Evidence shows minor dipping during local hours 00:00-01:00, but Oref1 low temp automation safely handles this without requiring basal rate reduction.
Appropriate morning transition rate supported by stable early morning glucose averages.
Adequately covers morning rise and dawn phenomenon without excessive hypoglycemia.
Maintains stable mid-day glucose levels with solid time in range.
Provides baseline coverage during afternoon hours; afternoon elevations are driven by unannounced intake or GLP-1 dynamics rather than basal deficiency.
Maintains smooth evening transition.
Appropriate evening basal delivery supporting stable nighttime entry.
Operating under a pure UAM/uncarbed strategy; current carb ratios are well-tolerated by closed-loop microbolusing.
Maintains appropriate insulin-to-carb scaling during early morning hours.
Appropriate daytime carb ratio supporting robust closed-loop performance.
Matches afternoon sensitivity needs when handling unannounced meals.
Maintains evening carb ratio stability.
Static ISF combined with dynamic sensitivity adjustment (70%) successfully modulates insulin sensitivity in real-time.
Maintains a safe overnight target consistent with high time in range.
Appropriate daytime target balancing glycemic control and hypoglycemia avoidance.
Safe evening target supporting stable overnight transitions.
10-hour duration of insulin action provides a protective buffer against insulin stacking when utilizing frequent SMBs and UAM.
Both SMB and UAM are correctly enabled, driving effective closed-loop microbolusing and unannounced meal recovery.
Activation settings correctly support an uncarbed/UAM operational workflow.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery cadence and basal limits provide well-balanced titration pacing.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Conservative wide safety limits prevent algorithmic restriction during corrections while maintaining safe ceilings.
Dynamic sensitivity successfully adapts ISF in real-time, eliminating the need for static Autosens.
7-hour max absorption window properly accommodates prolonged digestion patterns and GLP-1 therapy effects.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The system operates under a pure UAM and microbolus strategy with zero recorded carb entries, relying on Oref1 UAM detection, SMBs enabled always, and dynamic sensitivity (70%) to manage glucose excursions and GLP-1-induced delayed absorption.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain active SMB and UAM closed-loop automation with a 7-hour max absorption window. If tighter postprandial control is desired, initiate consistent carbohydrate logging and pre-meal bolusing to enable COB-based delivery.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log explicit carbohydrate amounts and timestamps for 3-5 meals to evaluate whether enabling COB-based SMB delivery improves postprandial peak control.

exceptions.pattern: Late afternoon glucose elevations during local hours 15:00-17:00
exceptions.suggestion: Review afternoon activity or consider temporary targets if unannounced late-day intake occurs.
exceptions.rationale: Coincides with active afternoon periods and potential GLP-1 pharmacokinetic fading or unannounced afternoon nutrition.

exceptions.pattern: Mild nocturnal dipping during local hours 00:00-01:00
exceptions.suggestion: Monitor overnight low trends closely and verify absence of insulin stacking.
exceptions.rationale: Oref1 low-temp enactments successfully prevent severe hypoglycemia, but slight dipping warrants ongoing observation.

implementation_steps: Verify current CGM coverage and data continuity to ensure reliable automated loop function.
Monitor overnight low trends (local hours 00:00-01:00) for one week to ensure Oref1 low-temp enactments continue to manage mild dipping safely.
Observe afternoon glucose trajectories (local hours 15:00-17:00) while noting any unannounced meal or snack intake.
If desired, begin logging a subset of meals with explicit carb amounts to test transition from pure UAM to COB-supported closed-loop delivery.
education: UAM (Unannounced Meal) detection allows Oref1 to respond to unexpected glucose rises without requiring manual meal carb entries.
Dynamic sensitivity automatically adjusts effective ISF based on recent glucose momentum, helping compensate for flat static ISF profiles.
Prolonged carbohydrate absorption settings (such as a 7-hour max absorption window) help accommodate delayed gastric emptying associated with GLP-1 therapy.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
